canonical; absorbs page-move-carries-sidecars (inverse direction of same bitmap-vs-sidecar invariant)
merged_body:
Page bitmap is the AUTHORITATIVE source of truth for byte-level symbolic-vs-concrete state in SymbolicMemory, NOT symbolic_objects/symbolic_spans. The sidecar maps (symbolic_objects, symbolic_spans, multi_objects) are caches/indexes that can lag behind page-bitmap-driven state. store_concrete's page.store_concrete correctly clears the bitmap bits but does NOT clean wider-sym sidecar entries based at a different address. Any load fast path that returns a sym (or extract) without first verifying the bitmap is buggy. See bytes_all_marked_symbolic helper (memory/mod.rs angr-jvjf) for the bitmap consultation pattern.

COROLLARY for merge repair loops (angr-fs8kb.68). SymbolicMemory::merge's trailing adopt-from-other backfill iterates other.symbolic_objects keyed at each object's BASE address. Gating that repair on `Entry::Vacant` at the base key is wrong: OCCUPIED != RESOLVABLE. The both-present per-byte walk earlier in merge legitimately overwrites the base key with a fresh 8-BIT ITE, so for an object straddling a page boundary (base page both-present, tail page other-only) the Vacant test fails and the tail bytes' symbolic_spans inserts are skipped entirely — bitmap-symbolic with no sidecar resolving them, load errors out. Two generalizable rules: (1) the resolvability predicate is per byte, `SymbolicMemory::symbolic_byte_lane(...).is_some()`, never `map.contains_key(base)`; (2) you cannot repair by re-pointing symbolic_spans at the base — symbolic_byte_lane rejects a span whose recorded width disagrees with the base object's actual width — so install an 8-bit self-referential entry per byte, the same shape the both-present walk uses. Gate the repair on the bitmap (this memory) AND on the byte not being Multi (see [[invariant-multi-vs-symbolic-cell-states]]), or you manufacture the inconsistent fourth cell state. Behavioural coverage lives in memory/tests/merge_sidecars.rs; this is the third recurrence of the adopt-the-bitmap-forget-the-sidecar shape after angr-c7xno.50 (multi_objects) and angr-91vj9.3 (interior symbolic_spans).

MOVE DIRECTION (inverse corollary, angr-c7xno.50): the bitmap is authoritative for READS but NOT self-sufficient for MOVES. MemoryPage carries only data + symbolic_bitmap + multi_bitmap; the per-address payloads (SymbolicMemory::symbolic_objects, symbolic_spans, multi_objects, multi_versions) are FLAT maps on SymbolicMemory, not nested in the page — so any path that inserts/clones/adopts a whole page from another SymbolicMemory (merge's (None,Some(op)) arm, snapshot restore, migration, prefetch) must copy the matching side-table entries explicitly or it installs bitmap bits pointing at nothing. Orphaned Multi bits are especially bad: range_has_multi (load.rs) gates on multi_objects, NOT the bitmap, so the load silently returns the stale concrete byte, and merge's 's_multi implies a payload' expect panics on the next merge. Fixed for merge by walking MemoryPage::multi_offsets (mirrors symbolic_offsets) and routing payloads through the existing multi_ops queue so set_multi_alternatives does the bitmap sync + bump_multi_version.

merged_body:
panic=abort makes any Python-supplied size a PROCESS-ABORT vector, not a catchable error. native/angr/Cargo.toml sets [profile.release] panic="abort", so nothing below is recoverable at the PyO3 boundary. Two shapes seen so far: (1) rangemap::RangeMap::{insert,remove} assert!(range.start < range.end), so an 'address..address + size' built from Python values without a checked_add guard aborts -- fixed in SegmentList::release (native/angr/src/segmentlist.rs, angr-9ke6b.199); SegmentList::occupy already had it. Convention: 'let Some(end) = address.checked_add(size) else { return; }' tagged // SILENT(cat-a), since a wrapping range describes no real region. (2) allocating a buffer whose length came straight from Python -- Vec's 'capacity overflow' panic near usize::MAX and handle_alloc_error for a merely huge size both abort. Fixed in Icicle::mem_read (native/angr/src/icicle.rs) via the free fn checked_read_len: reject a wrapping addr+size and a size above Icicle::max_mem_read_bytes (the mmu's own capacity()*page_size()), THEN allocate. Rule for new code: validate the range/length before you build it, whether the consumer is a RangeMap or the allocator; a free fn taking (addr, size, max) keeps it unit-testable where the surrounding type needs a VM/GIL.

COUNT-BEFORE-RESERVE (third shape, generalized): any Vec::with_capacity / reserve whose count crosses the PyO3 boundary must be bounded BEFORE the reservation — no guest input needed, an ordinary documented Python call (RustExplorationManager::register_simprocedure with a bogus num_args) is enough. Two fix shapes, pick by whether the refusal should degrade or raise. (a) Degrade: a named MAX_* const next to the error enum + a new error variant returned before the reservation, so the caller falls back (native dispatcher -> Python SimProcedure) instead of crashing — arch::MAX_EXTRACT_ARGS / ExtractionError::TooManyArgs guarding exploration::helpers::extract_args_with_abi (angr-0jh0j.23). (b) Raise at the trust boundary: a MAX_* const + a check_*(op, n) -> Result<(), String> guard called by every Python-facing entry point, message-typed rather than error-typed so the layer defining it stays pyo3-free and callers reporting through different channels (PyValueError vs BridgeError) can share it — symbolic::width_guards::check_bv_width is the precedent, symbolic::bv_chunk::check_concrete_load_size / MAX_CONCRETE_LOAD_BYTES the second instance (angr-0jh0j.11). Shape (b) is what a *generic* helper wants when it cannot construct its own error type E: guard at the boundaries, and additionally cap the helper's own reservation (Vec::with_capacity(n.min(MAX)) — bounds the allocation without truncating the result) as defence in depth. A bound like this also retroactively makes downstream index arithmetic (i * ptr_size) provably non-overflowing.

PyO3 'multiple-pymethods' IS now enabled in this project (native/angr/Cargo.toml pyo3 features = [py-clone, abi3-py310, multiple-pymethods], angr-9ke6b.50). A pyclass may have MANY #[pymethods] impl blocks, in any module in the crate. RustExplorationManager's ~228-method surface is split across manager_methods.rs (construction/config/callbacks) + manager_methods_{hooks,state,constraints,procedures,techniques,export,run,diagnostics,snapshot}.rs, one #[pymethods] block each, all opened with 'use super::*;'. The old (A)/(B) workarounds in pyo3-pymethods-child-module-split are no longer forced -- you may now peel a cohesive method group into its own file+block directly. Two costs the flip carries, both handled: (1) it pulls in the 'inventory' crate (linker-section class registration) and pyo3 documents a compile-time cost; (2) SURPRISE -- see below.

UNREACHABLE_PUB UNMASKING (angr-9ke6b.50): enabling the feature unmasked 391 unreachable_pub warnings crate-wide (lib.rs has #![warn(unreachable_pub)] from angr-9ke6b.214), instantly reddening CI clippy -D warnings. Mechanism: pyo3's NON-multiple-pymethods codegen was masking the lint on every #[pymethods] method AND on the #[pyclass] struct those blocks belong to — the flip does not create over-broad pubs, it reveals pre-existing ones. FIX CHOSEN: a scoped #[allow(unreachable_pub, reason = "pyo3 ...")] on each affected #[pymethods] impl block and #[pyclass] struct, restoring exactly the pre-feature coverage. Note the pyclass STRUCT needs its own allow separately from its #[pymethods] block. Rejected: rewriting ~391 'pub fn' -> 'pub(crate) fn' (mixes concerns, risks a dead_code wave). Do NOT blanket-allow unreachable_pub at crate level; that kills the guardrail for real Rust API surface.

CONVENTION for any NEW pyo3 item that trips the lint: use the scoped allow with the VERBATIM reason string used in segmentlist.rs/solver.rs — do NOT narrow it to pub(crate). Those items are reached from Python, not Rust, so their Rust visibility is decorative. Narrowing also makes clippy green, so the wrong fix is easy to land; check the existing allow sites before choosing. Non-pyo3 items keep the opposite rule (narrow to pub(crate), angr-9ke6b.214) so dead_code can see them.

merged_body: invariant: a test whose whole assertion is 'nothing happened' (a defensive/no-op branch, an ignored ping, a guard that returns early) must be proven non-vacuous before commit — temporarily invert the input so the branch is NOT taken and confirm the test fails, then restore. Same reasoning as the valgrind/rounding-mode gates' --self-test (CLAUDE.md): an assertion that has never been seen to fail is indistinguishable from one that cannot. Worked example: exploration/scheduler_tests.rs::test_wake_worker_out_of_range_id_is_noop asserts PersistentPool::wake_worker with worker_id past job_txs' end emits no upstream WorkerUp within 250ms; swapping the out-of-range ids for 0 must (and does) fail the recv_timeout assert, because a woken worker re-parks and emits a second Quiesced. Without that step the timeout would also 'pass' if the pool were simply dead. SECOND SHAPE (operand choice, angr-0jh0j.40/.43): overflow-guard regression tests must pick operands whose WRAPPING product/sum is benign, not merely huge — otherwise the test passes under both spellings and pins nothing. For a saturating_mul size*count guard, u64::MAX*2 is wrong (wraps to u64::MAX-1, still over the cap, so the oversize branch fires either way); 2^63*2 is right (wraps to exactly 0, which takes the zero-total early-return and reports a successful no-op for a 2^64-byte request). Canonical pair: procedures/fwrite_tests.rs::test_fwrite_size_times_nmemb_saturates_instead_of_wrapping and procedures/fread_tests.rs::test_fread_size_times_nmemb_saturates_instead_of_wrapping. Always mutation-check: swap saturating_mul -> wrapping_mul, confirm the new test FAILS, revert. Release builds set no overflow-checks so the wrapping result is what ships; a checked-profile panic is a second, weaker net.

merged_body: Before adding or trusting an IROp arm in native/angr/src/vex/opcode_map.rs or its opcode_map_float.rs / opcode_map_vector.rs siblings (angr-fs8kb.20 moved parse_float/parse_transcendental and parse_vector/parse_vreverse/parse_neon_unimplemented out of the parent), grep native/angr/vendor/pyvex_ffi.h for the exact Iop_ string — it is the vendored libVEX opcode enum and therefore the ground truth for what a real lift can emit. Two whole families were dead code that read as implemented coverage until angr-9ke6b.161/.162 (commit bad76646f): scalar Iop_MulHi{32,64}{S,U} (only vector Iop_MulHi<w>{U,S}x<n> exist; x86 IMUL/MUL lift to Iop_MullS32/Iop_MullU32 + Iop_64HIto32) and scalar Iop_Neg{8,16,32,64} (only float Iop_NegF32/Iop_NegF64 -> IROp::FNeg, the unmappable Iop_NegF128 -- IRType has no F128 variant -- and vector Iop_Neg32Fx2/Iop_Neg32Fx4/Iop_Neg64Fx2 exist; there is NO Iop_NegF16, so do not re-copy the old Iop_Neg{F16,F32,F64,F128} brace-enumeration this memory used to carry, corrected in angr-fs8kb.19; integer negation lifts as 0-x via Iop_Sub). The tell for this class: an opcode_map arm whose IROp variant has zero references in any *_tests*.rs — parse_opcode falls through to IROp::Unmapped for a name nobody emits, so the arm never fires and no test ever notices. The QDMulHi/QRDMulHi high-half vector family is genuinely unmapped (libVEX does emit Iop_QDMulHi*/Iop_QRDMulHi*; see the comment in vex/opcode_map_vector.rs and the opcode_map_tests.rs pins), which is a different thing from unreachable. Its widening sibling IS mapped: Iop_QDMull16Sx4/32Sx2 (NEON VQDMULL, (I64,I64)->V128) -> IROp::VQDMull, implemented by VEXOps::vec_qdmull (vex/ops/vec_permute_mul.rs: vec_mull lane layout + *2 + signed saturation, which only fires on MIN*MIN; the symbolic path widens to out_width+2 bits before doubling). The mirror-image shape also exists and is INTENTIONAL: an IROp variant that is fully implemented and tested but has no opcode_map producer because libVEX has no such opcode. IROp::ModS/ModU (no Iop_Mod* exists; guests use the combined Iop_DivMod*, and VEXOps::divmod_double_to_single takes its remainder straight from RustBV::urem/srem) and the bare 1-bit IROp::FCmp{EQ,LT,LE} (every real float compare carries a width/lane suffix -> FCmpScalarLane/FCmpVecPacked; suffix-free Iop_CmpF32/64 is the three-way FComCC and suffix-free Iop_CmpEQ8/16/32/64 are integer) are both documented as such at their ops_def.rs definition sites since angr-fs8kb.17/.18 — do not re-file them as dispatch gaps, and document any new one the same way.
